transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

Er03 on AEG induction hobs means "something is covering the control panel." A pasta boil-over is the classic cause. Starchy water on the touch controls is read as a finger permanently pressing a button, so the hob beeps and shuts itself off as a safety measure.

### How to fix it

1. Leave the hob off and let it cool for a few minutes. Remove all pans.
2. Wipe the control panel area thoroughly with a damp cloth, then dry it completely with a clean, dry towel. Starchy pasta water leaves a sticky, slightly conductive film, so:
• Wipe it a second time with a little washing-up liquid or ceramic hob cleaner to remove the starch residue.
• Dry again, paying attention to the edges of the glass and around the frame.
3. Check nothing is resting on the controls, such as a utensil, tea towel, or pan handle.
4. Switch the hob back on. The error should clear.

### If Er03 keeps coming back

Water may have seeped under the glass edge or into the hob's electronics.

• Turn off power to the hob at the fuse box/isolator switch (not just the hob's own button).
• Leave it off for several hours, ideally overnight, so any moisture can evaporate.
• Restore power and try again.

### If it still persists after drying out

The touch control board may have been damaged by liquid. Contact AEG service (or a qualified appliance engineer) rather than opening the hob yourself, since it's hard-wired to the mains. Have the model number (IKB64301FB) and the serial/PNC number ready. These are on the rating plate underneath the hob and usually on a sticker in the manual.

Tip for next time: if a boil-over happens, the hob will often switch off automatically. Wipe up the spill from the control area as soon as it's safe to do so, before the starch dries.

Ok, there was starchy water across the slider. I've wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes, and it works now. A wooden spoon was resting on the edge too, so I moved that. Is that all it needed?

Yes, almost certainly. You had two likely triggers, and you've dealt with both:

• The starchy water on the slider. The touch controls read that as a finger held down.
• The wooden spoon on the edge. If it was touching the control area, it can do the same thing, especially if it was damp.

Since the hob is working normally now, no further action is needed.

Worth keeping an eye on over the next day or so:

• Sticky film. If the slider feels sticky or responds erratically, give it another wipe with a drop of washing-up liquid or hob cleaner, then dry it. Dried starch can leave a residue that's hard to see.
• Er03 coming back on its own with nothing on the controls. That would suggest some water got under the glass edge. Switch off at the isolator overnight to let it dry fully. If it still recurs after that, it's one for an engineer.

To avoid a repeat, keep utensils and tea towels off the front edge where the controls are.
